correctness.rationale: Nondegenerate binary trace pairing yields precise fiber sizes; for rank m-1, zero pattern has one witness and nonzero patterns have 2-element cosets, proving the pair-sum obstruction. Every surviving kernel corresponds to exactly a_{m-1,m-1} supports. For rank m-2 only the unique nonzero kernel triple can be removed by three erasures. Lower supports have >3 witnesses per trace. The sharp threshold bounds follow by pair counting and complementary subspaces. Two independently generated cyclic recurrence checks replayed all 35 and 455 triple deletions at degrees 3 and 4, plus degree-5 tests.

value.rationale: Cyclic maximum-length sequences are canonical structured pseudorandom families. Exact rank-m-1 fragility under arbitrary phase erasures, plus the dependent/independent triple tradeoff of top vs penultimate faces, determines a natural structural robustness invariant not captured by VC dimension or the known full-array independence condition. Its link to projective one-saturating sets supplies a clear motivation and mathematical boundary for phase deletion. Missing-run experimental design literature supplies a separate motivated setting, but no design-optimality claim is made.
